content:
"Northern Territory police are facing severe criticism after a coroner's report revealed a pattern of negligence that allegedly contributed to the death of 23-year-old Dale Scott Walkinshaw last year. The report by NT coroner Greg Cavanagh details how police failed to implement crucial safety recommendations for caged vehicles, despite a history of self-harm and suicide attempts within them.

An internal report from 2013 had specifically recommended the installation of CCTV cameras in these vehicles, a suggestion that was seemingly ignored. In the three years leading up to Walkinshaw's death, at least 16 individuals attempted suicide in the confines of police vans. Alarmingly, Cavanagh's findings indicate that in six of these cases, the individuals were not discovered until they were in a critical state of semi-consciousness or unconsciousness. The coroner starkly concluded that it was "a matter of if a person would die in the back of a police van but when."

The tragic events unfolded on September 16th of last year. Two officers, en route to investigate a noise complaint in Darwin, stumbled upon the scene of a severe car crash. A Toyota Hilux had collided violently with a palm tree at the intersection of the Stuart Highway and Bargot Road, a location not far from Darwin airport. Behind a screen of vegetation, Dale Scott Walkinshaw, aged 23, was found. While Walkinshaw himself appeared physically unharmed, he was cradling his passenger. This young woman, whom he had met earlier at a bar, was suffering from an injury to her back and was drifting in and out of consciousness. Investigations later revealed that Walkinshaw was significantly over the legal blood alcohol limit, with a reading of 0.149."
